name: Clotrimazole
executiveSummary: Imidazole topical azole. Skin (tinea/candida): **1% cream q12h × 2–4 weeks**. Vaginal: **500 mg ovule once** or **100 mg nightly × 3–7 days**. Oral (oropharyngeal lozenges): **10 mg q5h** while awake × 7–14 days.
indications:
## Indications

- Dermatophytosis, cutaneous candidiasis, pityriasis versicolor.
- Vulvovaginal candidiasis.
- Oropharyngeal candidiasis (troches where available).

## Precautions

- Topical/mucosal only per presentation — not a substitute for systemic azoles in invasive disease.
- Vaginal: some oils affect latex condoms.
- Pregnancy: prefer short topical vaginal courses per obstetric advice.

> Continue skin treatment a few days after lesions clear.

adulto.presentation: Cream/solution 1%; ovules 100–500 mg; vaginal tabs; 10 mg oral lozenges (by country).
adulto.dose: Skin: **q12h** (sometimes q8–12h) × **2–4 weeks**. Vaginal: **500 mg once** or **200 mg × 3 nights** or **100 mg × 6–7 nights**. Oral troche: **10 mg dissolved q5h** (~5/day) × 7–14 days.
adulto.administration: Thin layer on clean skin; vaginal at bedtime; lozenge: dissolve in mouth, do not chew/swallow whole.
adulto.notes: Athlete’s foot: continue ≥2 weeks after improvement.

pediatrico.dose: Skin: **q12h** as adult. Vaginal/oral lozenges: by age and label (often adolescents/adults).
pediatrico.notes: Diaper candidiasis: thin layer after hygiene; treat reservoirs.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Burning, pruritus, local erythema; rare: contact allergy.
